newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica govt debt/GDP ratio at 55pct in '97 - Manuel.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica govt debt/GDP ratio at 55pct in '97 - Manuel.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Tuesday he expected the government debt to GDP ratio to reach its lowest level in over six years in 1997.

"We...expect government debt to come down from 58 percent of GDP in the second half of 1995 to below 55 percent in 1997 - a fall in this ratio for the first time in over six years," he told the Societe Generale Frankel Pollak annual investment conference.

Manuel reaffirmed his commitment to achieving a 1997/98 budget deficit of four percent in the forthcoming budget, due to be presented on March 12, with a reduction to three percent by the end of the century, from 5.1 percent in 1996/97.
A strong inflow of foreign capital during the first six weeks of this year had contributed to bringing bond rates down below 15 percent for the first time since March 1996, he noted.
"A lower public sector borrowing requirement in 1997/98 will reinforce this downward trend in interest rates," he said.

Manuel said the South African economy was currently going through a "mild slowdown", but the government anticipated a growth recovery towards the end of 1997, which would be sustained and strengthened during the remaining years of the decade.
The economy's potential had for decades been suppressed by discrimination, regulatory constraints and a series of unproductive industrial investments.

"This is behind us. We will enter the twenty first century a robust, revitalised, rapidly industrialising powerhouse of the southern African region, capable of taking full advantage of the opportunities the global economy offers," Manuel said.
